newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan to visit Britain, France and Netherlands.
newsitem.headline: Annan to visit Britain, France and Netherlands.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan will make a week-long trip to Britain, France and the Netherlands next week that will include meetings with heads of state and government leaders, a U.N. spokesman said on Thursday.

Annan, who took office on Jan. 1, visited Washington last month. His only trip abroad as secretary-general has been to an economic conference at Davos, Switzerland, and to the U.N. European headquarters in Geneva.

He is scheduled to arrive in London on Feb. 25. His itinerary there includes an audience the following morning with Queen Elizabeth at Buckingham Palace and meetings with Prime Minister John Major, Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind and former Foreign Secretary Douglas Hurd.

On Feb. 26 he attends the unveiling by the Queen at a West London synagogue of a memorial to Raoul Wallenberg, the Swedish diplomat who saved tens of thousands of Jews from the Nazis in Hungary during the Second World War. Wallenberg was an uncle of Annan's Swedish wife, Nane.
On Feb. 27 Annan will meet Israeli President Ezer Weizman, who will also be in London, and hold talks with the leader of Britain's opposition Labour Party, Tony Blair.
Shortly after arriving in Paris on the afternoon of Feb. 27 Annan will confer with Prime Minister Alain Juppe.

On Feb. 28 he has meetings with Foreign Minister Herve de Charette; Defence Minister Charles Millon; Senate foreign affairs committee chairman Xavier de Villepin; National Assembly foreign affairs committee chairman Valery Giscard d'Estaing; and Environment Minister Corinne Lepage.
On March 1 he will be received by President Jacques Chirac and later hold talks with the director-general of the Paris-based U.N. Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation, Federico Mayor.

Annan arrives at The Hague on March 2. His itinerary includes an audience with Queen Beatrix and meetings with Prime Minister Wim Kok, Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo and Minister for Development Cooperation Jan Pronk.

While at The Hague the secretary-general will also meet judges and officials of both the International Court of Justice, the U.N.'s principal judicial arm, and of the U.N. War Crimes tribunal on the former Yugoslavia.
He flies back to New York on March 4.
